classification.difficultyReason: Read marked angle boundaries and name each angle with its vertex in the middle.

content.prompt: Name each angle indicated in the diagrams below.

spec.description: Three segments OA, OB and OC; only the sector between OA and OB is marked. Ordinary source blue strokes are black under house style.
spec.mathematics: O is the common vertex; OB lies inside angle AOC.

answer.worked: The marked arc joins $OA$ and $OB$. Its vertex is $O$, so the angle is $\angle AOB$ (or $\angle BOA$).

spec.description: Rectangle LMNO with diagonal OM. The arc at O marks LOM; the full corner arc at M crosses OM and marks LMN. Ordinary strokes are black.
spec.mathematics: The M arc extends from ML to MN, not merely to MO.

answer.worked: At $O$, the marked arc joins $OL$ and $OM$, giving $\angle LOM$. At $M$, the arc extends from $ML$ to $MN$ across the diagonal, giving the whole angle $\angle LMN$.

spec.description: Segments VF, VG and VH, with VG inside the marked whole angle FVH. Ordinary strokes are black.
spec.mathematics: One continuous arc crosses VG and terminates on VF and VH.

answer.worked: The arc spans $VF$ to $VH$, crossing $VG$. The vertex is $V$, so the whole marked angle is $\angle FVH$ (or $\angle HVF$).

spec.description: AB and CD cross at M; the upper arc joins MA to MD. Ordinary strokes are black.
spec.mathematics: A, M, B are collinear; C, M, D are collinear.

answer.worked: The upper arc joins $MA$ and $MD$. With vertex $M$ in the middle, the marked angle is $\angle AMD$ (or $\angle DMA$).

spec.description: A, L, M, B lie on one line in that order. LX rises left and MY rises right. The M arc spans the entire upper straight angle across MY. Ordinary strokes are black.
spec.mathematics: Marked angles are ALX and LMB; MY does not terminate the M arc.

answer.worked: At $L$, the arc joins $LA$ and $LX$, giving $\angle ALX$. At $M$, the semicircular arc runs from $ML$ to $MB$ across $MY$, giving the straight angle $\angle LMB$.

spec.description: Circle with boundary order P, Q, R, S clockwise and chords SP, SQ, SR, PR, QR. The S arc joins SP to SQ; the R arc joins RS to RQ across RP. Ordinary strokes are black.
spec.mathematics: Marked angles are PSQ and SRQ. The circle has no given centre or measurements.

answer.worked: At $S$, the arc lies between $SP$ and $SQ$, giving $\angle PSQ$. At $R$, the arc spans $RS$ to $RQ$ across $RP$, giving the whole angle $\angle SRQ$.
